definitions.explanation: A wall or boundary fence built of stones, often surrounding a traditional house, temple, or castle grounds. Older and more decorative than concrete block walls.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{石塀|いしべい}が{残|のこ}っている。
{城下町|じょうかまち}には{立派|りっぱ}な{石塀|いしべい}が{並|なら}んでいる。
examples.english: Splendid stone walls line the streets of the castle town.

examples.japanese: {京都|きょうと}の{古|ふる}い{町並|まちな}みでは、{苔|こけ}の{生|は}えた{石塀|いしべい}が{独特|どくとく}の{雰囲気|ふんいき}を{生|う}み{出|だ}している。
examples.english: In Kyoto's old townscape, moss-covered stone walls create a distinctive atmosphere.

notes:
Compound of {石|いし} (stone) + {塀|べい} (wall, fence). Carries a more traditional, weathered image than its modern counterpart, ブロック{塀|べい}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {古|ふる}い{石塀|いしべい}: old stone wall
- {石塀|いしべい}に{囲|かこ}まれる: be enclosed by a stone wall
- {苔|こけ}の{生|は}えた{石塀|いしべい}: moss-covered stone wall
- {石塀|いしべい}{沿|ぞ}いに{歩|ある}く: walk along a stone wall

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ブロック{塀|べい}: concrete block wall — modern, mass-produced equivalent
- {石垣|いしがき}: stone embankment — built from large stones, often around castles
- {築地塀|ついじべい}: traditional earthen-and-tile wall (around temples)
